title: perf(hibernate): drop clean caches and scale compression threads before snapshot
head: 257aa42345ec
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Existing hibernation installations never receive the new hook on upgrade
leads.consequence: The old resume marker makes setup (even --force) exit before install_root_file; replacing the package upgrades only /usr/share/omarchy/default/systemd/system-sleep/drop-caches, not the active /usr/lib hook. Normal hibernation on previously configured machines receives none of the proposed changes. Add a migration/backfill for already configured installations, or install/refresh the hook before the early exit, while preserving its hardware conditionality.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F1); corroborated; coordinator verified --force does not bypass marker check (setup:63 vs :79). Published.

leads.summary: Hibernation removal leaves the cache-dropping hook active
leads.consequence: After omarchy hibernation remove clears the resume marker and swap, the executable in /usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/drop-caches remains. A later systemctl hibernate using a separately configured swap still synchronizes and drops caches; removing hibernation does not undo this PR's persistent root hook. Remove the hook when removing Omarchy hibernation, while distinguishing user-owned replacements if appropriate.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F2); coordinator verified remove script. Published.

leads.summary: hybrid-sleep hibernates without executing either new preparation step
leads.consequence: systemctl hybrid-sleep produces a hibernation image, but systemd passes SYSTEMD_SLEEP_ACTION=hybrid-sleep. The equality check skips both the compression-thread setting and cache drop, so this hibernation path never receives the speedup. Match hybrid-sleep as well as hibernate if all image-writing paths are intended (but retain the suspend no-op).
leads.triage: already verified in Opus final (hook matrix); Omarchy exposes no hybrid-sleep path. Not published (low value).

leads.summary: Unconditionally setting nproc discards an administrator's compressor-thread cap
leads.consequence: On a supported kernel an administrator can set hibernate_compression_threads=1 (boot parameter or runtime sysfs) to limit compression CPU/memory use. A routine hibernation silently replaces it with nproc, even if the administrator chose a lower limit on purpose. Consider leaving an already customized nondefault value alone or providing an explicit opt-out. The kernel also caps actual workers at online CPUs minus one; nproc is not necessarily the number used.
leads.triage: new; factual; hook writes unconditionally (diff) and boot param sets same variable (Opus report swap.c:1696-1710; confirmed CORRECT in Opus self-check). Published as one sentence.

leads.summary: Ownership test and sleep-hook fixture omit the new installation
leads.consequence: The explicit hibernation-hook assertion and install-before-marker order test mention only keyboard-backlight. Removing/moving the new install_root_file lines after the marker would leave those assertions passing while making the new feature unavailable/non-retryable. Add destination/mode/order assertions for drop-caches and a stubbed action test that exercises pre hibernate, compound hibernate and suspend. The existing ownership test passes at head but is not proof the new copy is installed.
leads.triage: coordinator verified (unowned-system-paths-test.sh:148-151). Published as a clause in finding 2; no optional test note (no demonstrated mutation).

leads.summary: Live drop-caches hook is not package-owned despite PR description
leads.consequence: Both settings recipes package only the source under /usr/share/omarchy/default, and install only unmount-fuse directly at /usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep. The new live file is manually copied by setup, intentionally admitted by the hardware-conditional allowlist. Consequently pacman does not update/remove that copy, and a later package taking over the same live path will initially conflict unless a takeover is handled. Correct the claim 'package-owned under /usr/lib', or design an explicit ownership transition that preserves conditional installation.

leads.summary: System sleep file-layout reference omits the new conditional hook
leads.consequence: The file layout lists unmount-fuse as the package-owned live hook and explicitly enumerates conditional source-only hooks as force-igpu and keyboard-backlight. Add drop-caches to the latter enumeration and explain its install/remove behavior, so readers do not mistake its source package for a packaged active hook.
leads.triage: already in Opus nits; coordinator verified line 142 at head. Published in finding 2 suggested change.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the new `drop-caches` hook acts only on the `pre` phase of a hibernation, including the hibernate step of suspend-then-hibernate, and does nothing for suspend or `post`. A fresh `omarchy-hibernation-setup` run installs it at mode 755. The main gap is delivery: machines that already have hibernation configured never receive the hook, because setup exits before the new install step and the PR adds no migration. A few statements in the hook comment and PR description also overstate what the hook does or how it is managed.

**Verified hook behavior** (a copy of the hook with `/sys` and `/proc` paths redirected to private files, `sync` and `nproc` stubbed, `nproc` = 12, knob starting at 3):

| `$1 $2` | `SYSTEMD_SLEEP_ACTION` | Compression threads after | `drop_caches` written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pre hibernate` | `hibernate` or unset | 12 | 3 |
| `pre suspend-then-hibernate` | `hibernate` | 12 | 3 |
| `pre suspend-then-hibernate` | `suspend` | 3 | no |
| `pre suspend` | `suspend` | 3 | no |
| `post hibernate` | `hibernate` | 3 | no |
| `pre hibernate`, knob file absent or read-only | `hibernate` | unchanged | 3, exit 0 |

The head also merges cleanly with the current `quattro` tip, and the existing `unowned-system-paths-test.sh`, `config-test.sh` and `system-sleep-ownership-migration-test.sh` pass on it.

### Existing hibernation setups never receive the hook

`bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup` returns early when hibernation is already configured, before the new `install_root_file` call:

```text
omarchy-hibernation-setup (with or without --force)
├─ :63  omarchy_resume.conf contains HOOKS+=(resume)?
│    └─ yes → "Hibernation is already set up", exit 0   ← already configured machines stop here
└─ :118 install_root_file ... keyboard-backlight
   :123 install_root_file ... drop-caches                ← only reached on a fresh setup
```

A copy of the setup script with a stubbed `sudo` confirmed this: with the resume marker present it prints "Hibernation is already set up", makes no `sudo` calls and installs no hooks. `--force` does not change this, because the marker check runs before `--force` is used. No file under `migrations/` installs the new hook.

**Impact:** the Omarchy ISO installer runs hibernation setup by default, so machines installed from it on supported hardware already have the marker. They get the updated source under `/usr/share/omarchy`, but `/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/drop-caches` is never created by `omarchy update` or by re-running `omarchy hibernation setup`. Only new installs, or a full `omarchy hibernation remove` followed by setup (which recreates the swapfile), get the change. A factory reset restores the installer's snapshot, so it includes the hook only on machines installed with this change.

**Suggested change:** either add a migration that checks for the resume marker and installs the hook when it is absent (the staging helper in `migrations/1788662350.sh` can be reused, but that migration itself returns early when a hook is missing, so its flow cannot be copied as is), or ship the hook from the `omarchy-settings` package the way `unmount-fuse` is shipped. The hook does nothing outside hibernation, so installing it everywhere is harmless, and package ownership would also let later edits to the hook reach installed copies.

### Install and removal claims in the PR description

- **"Package-owned under `/usr/lib`, matching the existing sleep hooks":** `install_root_file` writes a file that no package owns, like `keyboard-backlight` and `force-igpu`. Only `unmount-fuse` is package-owned. Because pacman ignores the file, a later change to the hook source will not reach machines that already have it unless a migration copies it again.
- **"Removed by `omarchy-hibernation-remove`":** `bin/omarchy-hibernation-remove` does not touch `/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep`, so the hook stays after hibernation is removed. It still only acts on hibernate, so the leftover is harmless.
- **"Already allowlisted in `unowned-system-paths-test.sh`":** true, since the whole `/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep` directory is allowlisted. That test's explicit install assertions only check `keyboard-backlight`.

**Suggested change:** correct the description. If the hook stays setup-installed, remove it in `omarchy-hibernation-remove` and add it to the list of conditional hooks in `docs/file-layout.md:142`.

### Hook comment and measurements overstate the effect

- The hook comment says the cache drop "turns a ~70s CPU-bound stall into an instant shrink". The PR's own measurement is 72.66 s before and 57.15 s after, with the remaining time attributed to anonymous-page eviction into zram.
- The comment's reasoning, "the kernel discards clean caches anyway", may not hold under Omarchy's `vm.swappiness=150`, where reclaim favors anonymous pages over file cache. A plausible explanation for the gain is that dropping the cache up front saves compressing memory into zram. This is a reading of the kernel source (`mm/vmscan.c`), not a measurement.
- The `Allocated ... in` line cannot show any effect of `hibernate_compression_threads`, because image compression happens later, when the image is written. The kernel's `Using N thread(s) for lzo compression` and `Wrote ... kbytes in` lines would show it. The timing also leaves out the hook's own `sync` and cache drop, and the PR reports only a single before/after pair.
- Writing `nproc` gives nproc − 1 compression threads (the kernel uses `clamp(num_online_cpus() - 1, 1, value)`), so 11 on the 12-thread test machine, not 12 as the comment implies. The write also replaces any lower value set with the `hibernate_compression_threads=` boot parameter. The knob exists from Linux 6.19; on older kernels the `-w` guard skips it as intended.

**Suggested change:** correct the comment, and report a few runs of total hibernation entry time together with the `Wrote` and `Using N thread(s)` kernel lines.

**Optional:** `echo 3` drops clean, unused page cache plus reclaimable dentries and inodes on every hibernation, including light ones, whose snapshot allocation the author measured at 2.40 s without the hook. Anything dropped that is used again after resume has to be read from disk, and Omarchy's own sysctl comment for `vm.vfs_cache_pressure` calls the dentry and inode cache costly to rebuild. Comparing `echo 1` (page cache only), and measuring responsiveness after resume, would show whether the full drop is worth that cost.

---

**Test scope:** reviewed head `257aa423`. The hook and setup script were exercised only as path-redirected copies with stubbed `sync`, `nproc` and `sudo` in an isolated sandbox; no real hibernation, cache drop or sysfs write was performed. The performance claims were assessed from Linux 7.2 and systemd 262 source only, not measured on hardware.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
